topicName: Creating and Running an Angular Project (ng new, ng serve)
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Creating and Running an Angular Project (ng new, ng serve)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial will guide you through the process of creating a new Angular project using the Angular CLI (Command Line Interface) and running it locally using the 'ng new' and 'ng serve' commands."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Node.js and npm (Node Package Manager) must be installed on your system. You can download them from the official Node.js website."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Angular CLI: Install the Angular CLI globally using the following command: 'npm install -g @angular/cli'"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a New Angular Project (ng new)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 'ng new' command is used to create a new Angular project with a basic structure and configuration. Follow these steps:"},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"ng new my-angular-project"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace 'my-angular-project' with the desired name for your project. The CLI will prompt you with a few questions:"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Would you like to add Angular routing? (y/N): Choose 'y' if you want to include Angular routing in your project, otherwise choose 'N'."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Which stylesheet format would you like to use? Choose your preferred stylesheet format (CSS, SCSS, Sass, Less, Stylus)."},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"The CLI will then generate the project files and install the necessary dependencies. This process may take a few minutes."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Navigating to the Project Directory"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the project is created, navigate to the project directory using the 'cd' command:"},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"cd my-angular-project"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Running the Angular Project (ng serve)"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 'ng serve' command builds the application and serves it locally, allowing you to view it in your browser. Use the following command:"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"ng serve"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"This command will build the project and start a development server. By default, the application will be available at 'http://localhost:4200/'. You can open this URL in your browser to view the running application."},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can also specify a different port using the '--port' option:"},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"ng serve --port 8080"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"This will serve the application on port 8080 ('http://localhost:8080/')."},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 'ng serve' command also includes live reloading, which means that any changes you make to the project files will automatically be reflected in the browser."},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Additional ng serve Options"},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"--open or -o: Opens the application in your default browser automatically. Example: 'ng serve --open'"},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"--host: Specifies the host address to use. Example: 'ng serve --host 0.0.0.0' (allows access from other devices on the network)"},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"You have successfully created and run an Angular project using the 'ng new' and 'ng serve' commands. You can now start developing your application by modifying the project files in the 'src' directory."}]
